transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-11-30 15:00 PST
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood CSM), Sofia Martinez (Graystone Director of Data), Tom Lee (Platform Engineer), Hannah Cho (Security), Ibrahim Khan (Product)

Summary: Quick intros, high level goals (reduce inference cost, <150ms p95 for key routes, ensure PHI controls), security checklist, sandbox onboarding plan, assign owners and due dates.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — welcome to the Redwood onboarding kickoff for Graystone. I'm Jamie, I'll be your AE. Marco and Priya from our side too. How's everyone?
[00:08] Sofia Martinez: Hey Jamie, thanks, excited. We are looking to replace an in-house service and get predictable latency and cost. Primary use case is chart summarization and clinical note embeddings.
[00:18] Marco Ruiz: Nice, that's helpful. Marco here on the SE side — quick question Sofia, typical sequence lengths and qps for the pilot?
[00:25] Sofia Martinez: For pilot, sequences are usually 512 tokens for summaries, embeddings pipe is about 10k calls a day but spikes to 200 qps during morning batch processing, hmm sorry numbers are rough...
[00:40] Tom Lee: I'll send a proper histogram after the call, we have telemetry but it's a pain to export live.
[00:45] Marco Ruiz: Great, that histogram will help with kernel selection and batching suggestions.
[00:50] Priya Patel: On the onboarding process — we'll provision a sandbox org, share credentials and example prompts, and set up a joint workshop to run an initial baseline. That typically takes 1–2 weeks.
[01:02] Ibrahim Khan: What's the difference again between hosted and dedicated? We have regulatory constraints for some workloads.
[01:08] Jamie Chen: Good question. Hosted is fast to get started — API keys, multitenant, usage billing. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and data isolation, and Private (VPC/on-prem) is for strict compliance — we can support VPC peering, customer-managed KMS, and air-gapped options.
[01:24] Hannah Cho: On the compliance note — we need SOC 2 plus regional data residency for EU patients. Also SSO/SAML integration and audit logs for model calls.
[01:32] Priya Patel: We have SOC2 and ISO packages; we'll share the full security pack. For SAML/SO we support SSO and RBAC — auditing is available with token-level traces in Console.
[01:45] Hannah Cho: Great, and KMS/HSM integrations? Keys must be customer-managed.
[01:50] Marco Ruiz: Yes, we can integrate with AWS KMS and external HSMs via our Private deployment. For hosted we offer envelope encryption but if you require CMKs we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[02:05] Tom Lee: Cost question — if we start hosted for speed then move to dedicated after pilot, what does the migration look like? Any big breakage?
[02:12] Jamie Chen: We've done that for several customers — migration is mostly config and model pinning; API surface stays the same so application changes are minimal. We'll plan a canary and a short rollback window.
[02:24] Sofia Martinez: Timeline wise we want pilot in Jan, production by end of Q1. Is that realistic?
[02:29] Marco Ruiz: Yes — if we get sample data and your histograms this week, we can run baselines and sizing in early Dec, then pilot in Jan looks doable.
[02:36] Ibrahim Khan: Any required data residency paperwork?
[02:40] Priya Patel: We'll include contractual language in the SOW and can add region restrictions on hosted or plan for Private option if needed.
[02:47] Jamie Chen: Action items — we'll send SOW draft, security docs, and spin up sandbox. Marco will run perf tests with your samples; Tom will send artifacts.
[02:58] (crosstalk)
[03:01] Marco Ruiz: A note on perf — if your seq lengths are frequently >1024 we recommend certain kernel/quant settings; we'll test 8-bit quant to see latency/cost tradeoffs.
[03:12] Tom Lee: Okay noted, our longest sequences can hit 1500 in rare cases.
[03:17] Marco Ruiz: Good to know — that affects KV cache and memory planning.
[03:22] Hannah Cho: For security review, can you provide pen test reports and audit logging retention options?
[03:28] Priya Patel: Yes, pen test summary is in the security pack, and we support configurable retention for logs as an add-on.
[03:36] Sofia Martinez: Who should I expect to work with for the integration workshop?
[03:40] Jamie Chen: Marco will lead the SE workshop, Priya will coordinate, and I'll handle contracts and exec syncs.
[03:46] Ibrahim Khan: Any recommended throttling/batching defaults?
[03:50] Marco Ruiz: We'll suggest batching window and prefix caching; Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization profiles and autoscale policies based on your workload.
[04:00] Sofia Martinez: Sounds good. We'll prioritize PHI-sensitive routes for Private/Dedicated review.
[04:05] Jamie Chen: Understood. Next steps recap — Jamie to send the deck and SOW, Priya to send SOC2+security pack and invite to sandbox, Marco to run perf tests once Tom provides sample data.
[04:16] Tom Lee: I'll share traffic histograms and a small sanitized sample set by Friday.
[04:20] Hannah Cho: I'll compile the compliance questions and send them to Priya.
[04:25] Jamie Chen: Great — we'll block time for the integration workshop week of Dec 7. Any final Qs?
[04:30] Sofia Martinez: No, thank you all. Excited to get started.
[04:34] Jamie Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.

End of transcript.
